title: Casper and the Uniform
premise: In 1913 London, Elodie Blackwood drives for suffragist leader Verity Ashcombe and secretly reads every letter she delivers, convinced history is something that happens to other people. When an abandoned child wearing a soldier's uniform coat appears at their door with a note instructing them to forget his face, Elodie discovers he is the illegitimate son of a war hero whose family will erase him to protect a political legacy. Racing against the boy's powerful relatives and a government eager to bury wartime scandals, Elodie smuggles evidence into print and testifies before an inquiry, choosing at last to make herself part of history rather than its courier. The book ends with the truth on the record, the boy adopted into the movement's found family, and Elodie signing her own name to the account.
about_author: Juniper Underhill is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suffragist correspondence in regional collections across northern England. She writes historical fiction about the ordinary hands that carry history from one person to another.

chapters.title: The Letters I Was Never Meant to Keep
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. We meet her as Verity Ashcombe's driver: capable, invisible, quietly reading the mail she carries and telling herself it means nothing. A letter hints at scandal surrounding Colonel Fairhurst's war record. That night, a child in an oversized uniform coat is left on the doorstep with a note: forget this face. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into complicity — she keeps the note instead of burning it.

chapters.title: Forget This Face
chapters.summary: Alternating Elodie and the boy Casper's POV. Elodie traces the coat to Fairhurst's household; Casper slowly reveals fragments of the journey that brought him there. The Fairhursts' solicitor arrives with money and threats, insisting the child never existed. Verity hesitates — the movement cannot afford enemies. Emotional beat: Elodie realizes reading history isn't enough; someone must write it.

chapters.title: What the Victors Burn
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, rising tension. She steals copies of Fairhurst's letters proving Casper's parentage and the cover-up of a wartime atrocity, hiding them inside her delivery rounds while being followed by the solicitor's man. Verity is arrested at a protest, leaving Elodie alone with the boy and the evidence. Emotional beat: terror transformed into resolve — she decides to get everything on the record before the inquiry closes.

chapters.title: Signed, Elodie Blackwood
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, Elodie's POV. At the inquiry, Elodie presents the letters and names herself as their keeper, defying the Fairhursts' counsel; Casper, coached by the movement's women, speaks his own name aloud. The record stands, the cover-up collapses, and Verity returns to find her driver has become a witness. Emotional beat: belonging earned — Elodie stops delivering other people's histories and claims her own.
